conflicts.description: catalyst-junkie are long AONIA_2026-10 while mean-reverter are short

own_pitch.stance_summary: Verified: AONIA 4.35 overnight with October ASX IB implied 4.565 (+21.5bp) and November 4.685 (+33.5bp); NSW stamp-duty receipts -24% YoY and transactions -18% with Sydney/Melbourne values more than 7% below peak; AU gauges inflation 82 / activity 54 / labor 50 / consumer 48; AU 2Y 4.999 after a 1m +39.1bp selloff and a 1d -5.5bp dip. Inference: the dated October RBA window is still priced as a near-full hike even though the housing channel the RBA uses is already contracting, so the first liquid AONIA contract should reprice lower if the Board cannot deliver that hike. Unknown: the exact RBA calendar date inside the October contract and whether inflation 82 dominates housing in the reaction function. Express as long AONIA_2026-10 (receive), not AUDUSD.
own_pitch.thesis: Fact: the October AONIA contract still implies 4.565 against a 4.35 overnight after a 16 Sep housing print that shows the RBA tightening channel already biting. Inference: that is too much hike for a Board staring at falling turnover, a stamp-duty collapse and cooling activity/labor/consumer gauges, so the dated October decision is the mechanism that should reprice the contract lower if they hold. Unknown: whether inflation 82 is sufficient for them to hike through the housing evidence. Valuation without that meeting can stay wrong; the meeting is why this is a trade rather than a 99th-percentile AU 2Y fade.
own_pitch.mispricing: October IB prices about 21.5bp of tightening, i.e. a near-full 25bp hike, after new housing-volume and stamp-duty evidence that the transmission channel is already contracting. The market is assuming housing pain is compatible with another hike; the disagreement is that the next meeting cannot both acknowledge that channel and still deliver the priced 25bp.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: October AONIA still prices a near-full RBA hike after housing transmission has already broken, so the meeting should reprice that contract lower.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: October RBA decision against AONIA_2026-10 implied 4.565 after the 16 Sep housing print.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: RBA delivers the priced 25bp hike or inflation stays at gauge 82 while housing stabilizes.

opposing_pitches.stance_summary: Do not fade US 2Y just because it prints a 252-day high: it sits on the live SR3 path after a delivered, pre-priced hike with still-hot US gauges. The stretched object with a reversal condition is Australia: AU 2Y 4.999 as of 2026-09-16 sits through live AONIA (overnight 4.35; Oct-26 4.565; Mar-27 4.86; path peak 4.945) after 16 Sep housing evidence that the tightening channel is already biting. Fade the remaining 21-51bp of priced RBA hikes in the AONIA strip, not AUDUSD.
opposing_pitches.thesis: FACT: 16 Sep housing evidence shows NSW stamp-duty -24 percent y/y, volumes -18 percent, Sydney/Melbourne >7 percent off peak while AONIA still prices Oct-26 4.565 and Mar-27 4.86 from overnight 4.35, and AU 2Y 4.999 sits through that path. INFERENCE: crowded extrapolation of inflation-gauge 82 plus the delivered Fed hike has overshot the RBA's remaining hike capacity now that the housing channel is binding; the extra 21-51bp should be faded. UNKNOWN: positioning and the next CPI vintage. This is not a US 2Y fade and not an AONIA-easing call.
opposing_pitches.mispricing: The market prices another +21.5bp by Oct-26 and +51bp by Mar-27 in AONIA, and AU 2Y 4.999 is 13.9bp through Mar-27 AONIA 4.86, after housing volumes and prices have already broken. The 99th-percentile AU 2Y rank is the discovery flag, not the thesis. The mispricing is remaining hike premium versus a working tightening channel, versus the live AONIA path.

conflict_synopsis.primary_trade: short AONIA_2026-10 (receive AONIA Oct-Nov-Mar strip / AU rates down)
conflict_synopsis.core_view: Fade remaining RBA hike premium in AONIA because housing is already biting and AU 2Y sits through the live path; do not fade path-consistent US 2Y on percentile alone.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Australian housing/labor prints and RBA communication that the tightening channel is binding, so Oct-Mar AONIA hikes are not delivered.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: AONIA Oct-26 4.565 and Mar-27 4.86 hold or rise while housing/labor stop deteriorating, or a delivered October RBA hike reprices the strip higher.
